thread:
Maya: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — a few items on consumption policy we promised to clarify: staging/test billing, retry behavior, and temporary SLO exemptions for infra runs.

Eli: thanks — can you list the concrete questions? easier to answer.

Maya: 1) Are CI/staging workloads billed against customer credits? 2) Do retries count as separate token charges? 3) Can we exempt internal integration tests from org monthly quotas? 4) During planned maintenance windows, does burst capacity apply the same?

Sam: Short answers: CI/staging -> billed unless the request uses the internal invocation flag or an infra key. Retries -> treated as new requests so tokens count. Internal test exemptions -> yes, but must be whitelisted via ops ticket. Maintenance bursts -> allowed up to reserved pool, not unlimited.

Eli: Product note: we'll add an "internal usage" toggle in the Console that maps to the policy. ETA end of Q2.

June: Ops process: to get the whitelist, open an ops ticket with org_id, job names, and expected monthly volume. We'll require an owner and a short justification. No open-call blanket exemptions.

Lisa: Legal: for customers on Dedicated or Private deployments, any billing adjustments or exemptions need to be captured in an amendment. For hosted customers we handle via ops policy.

Maya: Example header to mark infra/internal calls (for infra keys only):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \
  -H \"X-Redwood-Invocation-Type: internal\" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4-small","input":"smoke test"}'
```

Sam: Ops/security note: the internal header must only be used with infra-scoped keys. Abuse or customer-facing use will auto-flag and revoke. We'll add telemetry alerts.

Eli: I'll post a short docs PR + a follow-up message in #release-notes with the console screenshot and the exact API header text.

Maya: Great — please also include the ops ticket template so teams know what to file. :thumbsup:
